# One-minute submission video: plan and script

Written at 15:05 on Nov 21. Chris answered the decisions at 15:14 (section 7, decisions.md 15:14). The build code is being written; narration, capture and the final render wait for Chris's go. It replaces the "One-minute video" table in [SUBMISSION_PLAN.md](SUBMISSION_PLAN.md), which predates "Plan with Neon" and the results table.

**What the video is:** 60 seconds of screen captures of the running app, driven by a script, with narration generated by Gemini text-to-speech and burned-in captions of the same words. Nobody films or records. Every app shot is the real app on the demo laptop. The made-up frames are a 4 s generated opening under the title (labelled "generated video" on screen) and the results and end cards, which are plain text cards.

**The move it shows:** move `20261121-133201` (two venue rooms filmed today: 52 items, 16 boxes; one clip and one photo per room). Neon takes it from two 26 ft trucks (score 91.5) to one (95.2) with no rule broken ([eval/RESULTS.md](../eval/RESULTS.md), table 2). The build uses the move as it is, with `who=Demo` on the phone pages; the 3D page and the models page still print its id and name (D6).

> **Changed at 15:45 (decision 15:45): the narration lines and the title, results and end cards are now written by Gemini 4 Carbon**, not by the coding agent. `python -m scripts.video.build --write-script` sends `scripts/video/brief.md` (what each shot shows, what its line covers, word limits) and the facts in `scripts/slides/brief.md`, checks word counts and numbers, and saves `scripts/video/script.json`. The lines in the table below were the first draft and are no longer used; the shots, times and word limits still are. The results numbers changed too: `eval/RESULTS.md` was rebuilt at 15:31 (16 of 16 against 3 of 16, after one checker rule was relaxed for small moves).

## 2. Narration, timed

**Speaking rate, measured:** one test sentence of 24 words on `gemini-3.8-flash-tts`, voice Charon, style "warm, calm and clear… unhurried", came back as 9.84 s (146 words a minute, about 2.4 words a second, counting about 0.3 s of silence the model leaves at each end). The clip is at `.cache/video/tts_test.wav` on the demo laptop for Chris to hear.

**Budget:** 119 words over 60 s. Each shot's line is generated as its own clip, so each clip can be measured against its own shot.

| Shot | Words | Expected clip at 2.4 words/s | Shot length | Room left |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | 10 | 4.2 s | 6 s | 1.8 s |
| S2 | 17 | 7.1 s | 8 s | 0.9 s |
| S3 | 18 | 7.5 s | 9 s | 1.5 s |
| S4 | 11 | 4.6 s | 6 s | 1.4 s |
| S5 | 15 | 6.3 s | 8 s | 1.7 s |
| S6 | 20 | 8.3 s | 9 s | 0.7 s |
| S7 | 19 | 7.9 s | 9 s | 1.1 s |
| S8 | 9 | 3.8 s | 5 s | 1.2 s |
| **Total** | **119** | **49.7 s** | **60 s** | **10.3 s** |

Each clip starts 0.2 s after its shot starts. That leaves a short breath between shots and about 10 s of quiet spread across the minute. Numbers are written as words ("thirteen", "fourteen") so the voice reads them the same way the captions show them; "3D" and "Gemini 4" read correctly in the test.

## 3. How the audio is generated

**Model and voice:** `gemini-3.8-flash-tts` (listed for our event key under v1beta and v1alpha at 15:10 today, and the one test call worked). Voice **Charon** ("informative") with the style *"warm, calm and clear, like a friend explaining a project; unhurried"*, which matches the tone of George's live pitch ([PITCH_NOTES.md](PITCH_NOTES.md): "warm, unhurried, conversational"). Fallback model: `gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts`, same voices.

**The request** (Interactions API, `v1beta`, as the `gemini-api-dev` skill documents it; one request per shot):

```python
interaction = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-3.8-flash-tts",
    input=[{"type": "user_input", "content": [{
        "type": "text",
        "text": "<the shot's line, verbatim>",
        "annotations": [{"type": "speech_metadata",
                         "style": "warm, calm and clear, like a friend explaining a project; unhurried"}],
    }]}],
    response_format={"type": "audio"},                     # unary reply is a complete WAV, 24 kHz mono 16-bit
    generation_config={"speech_config": [{"voice": "Charon"}]},
    store=False,
)
wav = base64.b64decode(interaction.output_audio.data)
```

The text field is read verbatim, so stage directions go only in `style`. A pause, if one is needed, is an inline `<short pause>` tag.

**Keeping to the repo rule (only `backend/llm/` imports a model SDK).** Add a job to `backend/llm/models.toml` when the build starts, not now:

```toml
[jobs.narrate]
model = "gemini:gemini-3.8-flash-tts"   # submission video narration (plan/VIDEO_SCRIPT.md)
api_version = "v1beta"
voice = "Charon"
style = "warm, calm and clear, like a friend explaining a project; unhurried"
```

and one method next to `generate_image` in `backend/llm/` (`Job.speak(text) -> bytes`, WAV) that makes the call above, logs it like every other call and caches it by text, voice and style, so a second build costs nothing. The video build calls `for_job("narrate").speak(line)` and never imports `google.genai`. The `gemini-api` CLI is not installed on the laptop, and its `tts` command does not send the `style` annotation, so the CLI is only a manual fallback (`gemini-api tts "<line>" --voice Charon --out s3.wav`).

The two test scripts used while planning (list the models, one TTS call) ran from a scratch folder outside the repo with the SDK imported directly. They are not in git.

**Checking each clip against its shot:** after generation the build reads each WAV's length (frames ÷ rate) and trims silence at both ends (ffmpeg `silenceremove`, threshold −40 dB). The rule is spoken length ≤ shot length − 0.5 s. If a clip is too long: (1) generate it once more with "a little brisker" added to the style; (2) if still over by 8% or less, speed it up with `atempo` (≤ 1.08, not audible); (3) otherwise stop and print the line to shorten. The build writes a table of line, words, clip length, shot length and margin, and fails if any margin is negative.

**What the key can reach (listed at 15:10):** `gemini-3.8-flash-tts`, `gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts`, `lyria-3.5` (music), `gemini-omni-1.2-flash` (video). All are Gemini API models; nothing needs Google Cloud. One difference from `models.toml`: `gemini-decision-1` is now listed under v1beta as well as v1alpha. The repo keeps `v1alpha` for the `decide` job, which is what we measured working; this note changes nothing.

## 4. How the footage is captured, with nobody filming

**Driver:** the Node script that took the slide screenshots (`.cache/video/shoot.mjs`, headless Chrome over the DevTools protocol, written today) grows two features and moves into the repo as `scripts/video/shoot.mjs`:

- **Real recordings, not only stills.** `Page.startScreencast` sends a JPEG for every frame Chrome paints, with a timestamp. The script saves frames and timestamps per shot; ffmpeg turns them into a 30 fps clip at the real speed. This shows the scrolls, the tap on "see or change", the 3D load playing and the Neon rounds appearing as they happen.
- **A still fallback per shot.** If a shot gets fewer than 10 frames (for example, if headless Chrome's software WebGL paints the 3D view too slowly), the script takes a still at the end of the shot instead, and the build adds a slow zoom (ffmpeg `zoompan`, about 4% over the shot). The stills route is the one that already worked for the slides.

**Sizes:**

| Shots | Page | Viewport (CSS px) | Device scale | Captured at |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S2, S3, S4 | `capture.html`, `review.html` | 390×844, mobile on | 2 | 780×1688, shown 1000 px tall |
| S5, S6 | `index.html` | 1280×720 | 1.5 | 1920×1080, shown 1700×956 |
| S7 | `models.html` | 1280×720 | 1.5 | 1920×1080, shown 1700×956 |
| S1, S7 card, S8 | text cards, small HTML files the build writes to `.cache/video/cards/` | 1920×1080 | 1 | captured by the same Chrome, so the fonts match |

**The moves inside each shot** (by visible text, so they survive layout changes): S2 scroll from top to the footer over 6 s; S3 click the element whose text starts "answered · see or change", scroll 3 answers; S4 click it again, scroll to the card with "added by you"; S5 select "Load Truck (1→N)", click "▶ Play", record until "Step 68 / 68"; S6 click `#btn-plan`, record 1 s, keep recording until `#planner-rounds` is visible (up to 90 s), then 2 s more; S7 load and hold.

**Speeding up and cutting, and saying so:** S5's load playback is sped up to fit 8 s and labelled "×N" (the real factor). S6's Neon wait is cut; the label gives the real number of rounds and seconds, read from the page. Nothing else is sped up.

**After capture the build checks the page text** (through the same DevTools connection) for the claims the narration makes, and stops if one fails: S2 footer "52 items + 16 boxes"; S5 header "2 × U-Haul 26 ft" and "0 rule violations"; S6 header shows one truck and "0 rule violations" (otherwise the alternative S6 line is used, and its TTS clip is generated as well).

## 5. How it is assembled: one command

```powershell
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m scripts.video.build
```

Files (written when the build starts): `scripts/video/shots.json` (the table in section 1: times, page, moves, line, alternative line), `scripts/video/shoot.mjs` (capture), `scripts/video/build.py` (everything else). Tools: the demo `.venv` (Python with `google-genai` through `backend/llm/`, `Pillow`, `imageio-ffmpeg`, whose ffmpeg 9.0.2 build on this laptop has `subtitles`/`ass`, `drawtext`, `zoompan`, `xfade`, `loudnorm`, `atempo`, `apad`), Node 24 (built-in `WebSocket`), Chrome at its usual path, and the demo API running on `127.0.0.1:8000`. Nothing new to install.

What the command does, in order:

1. **Opening clip** (D3): one `for_job("video_open").generate_video()` call, cached; 1–3 minutes, started first and in the background.
2. **Narration:** one `for_job("narrate").speak()` call per shot (8 calls, about 5 s each), cached; then the length check in section 3. This step does not need the footage, so it can run before capture.
3. **Capture:** `node scripts/video/shoot.mjs scripts/video/shots.json` against `127.0.0.1:8000` (not the tunnel), then the text checks in section 4.
4. **Per shot clip:** frames to a 30 fps clip, fit to the shot's exact length (hold the last frame if short, cut if long), placed on the 1920×1080 frame with the step label; the narration clip laid in at +0.2 s and padded with silence (`apad`) to the shot length.
5. **Join:** concatenate the parts with plain cuts; each shot's caption (its whole line, up to two lines) is drawn with Pillow in Segoe UI on a dark band at the bottom; the narration clips are mixed at their start times and normalised to −16 LUFS (`loudnorm`); H.264 `yuv420p` (bt709, every part tagged the same) and AAC 48 kHz, `+faststart`.
6. **Check the result:** `ffprobe` says 60.0 s ± 0.1; a contact sheet (one frame every 2 s) and a sheet of every item thumbnail that appears in S4, for Chris to look at before uploading.

Output: `.cache/video/out/pack-it-up-60s.mp4`, plus `contact_sheet.jpg`, `thumbs_sheet.jpg`, `narration_check.txt`. All under `.cache/`, which is git-ignored (so are `*.mp4`, `*.wav`, `*.jpg`).

**Status at 15:25:** the build code is written and pushed (`scripts/video/`, the `narrate` and `video_open` jobs, `speak()` and `generate_video()` in `backend/llm/`). `--dry` runs it end to end with no model calls (silent narration of the estimated length, no Neon click, the title card standing in for the opening): 60.00 s, 1,799 frames, about 90 s on this laptop, every page check passing except S6's one-truck check, which needs the Neon click. Not yet run for real: TTS through the job, the Omni opening, the Neon click inside the capture.

## 6. Build checklist and times

Upload by 4:30 means the build starts by **3:45**. The narration and capture code (sections 3 to 5) is the long part; footage and audio are quick.

| When | Step | Takes | If it fails |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3:30 | Chris answers D1–D4. Last call for George: anything that changes `capture.html`, `review.html`, `index.html` or `models.html` after 3:50 is not in the video | – | Defaults: Charon, no music, no generated footage, end card with both addresses |
| 3:45 | `run_demo.ps1 -Status` (the API must answer on 127.0.0.1); `git pull --rebase`; add the `narrate` job and `speak()` | 10 min | – |
| 3:45 | In parallel: `shots.json`, `shoot.mjs` screencast, `build.py` | 20 min | Use the stills path that already works (`shoot.mjs` as it is now + `zoompan`) |
| 3:55 | Generate the narration (step 2 only); Chris listens to one clip | 2 min | TTS refused or quota: `gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts`; then the `gemini-api` CLI by hand; last resort is captions only, no voice (nobody on the team records) |
| 4:05 | Capture (step 3), including one live "Plan with Neon" | 3–4 min | Neon slow or fails: use the alternative S6 line with the page's real result; footage claims fail: fix the line, not the footage |
| 4:09 | Assemble and check (steps 4 to 6) | 2–3 min | Cross-fades or captions break: plain cuts, captions off |
| 4:12 | Chris watches the MP4 and the two contact sheets: no faces, no names, numbers right | 4 min | – |
| 4:16 | One slot for a fix and a second render | 5 min | If not fixed by 4:20, upload what we have |
| 4:20 | Upload to YouTube, unlisted; title "Pack It Up · Gemini 4 NYC hackathon"; description with the disclosure line | 3 min | – |
| 4:23 | Wait for YouTube to process HD | up to 5 min | SD is enough for the form |
| 4:28 | Open the link in a private window; paste it into the form | 2 min | – |

**Hard fallback if nothing renders by 4:15:** the eight-slide judging deck already has the same story with real screenshots of move 133201. Export it as PowerPoint, add the eight narration WAVs (step 2) one per slide, and use PowerPoint's "Export → Create a Video". About 10 minutes. It needs the narration, which is one more reason to generate it first.

Writing the build code earlier (from about 3:20) would leave a real margin; it touches no footage and makes no model calls until it runs. That is D5.

## Privacy and what stays out of git

- No faces: the capture and review pages show only item crops (small furniture thumbnails) and filenames. Every thumbnail visible in S4 goes on `thumbs_sheet.jpg` for Chris to look at before upload. Of the cards checked at 15:15 (desks, armchairs, sideboard, shelving cabinet), none showed a person.
- Names: the phone pages use "Demo" as the sign-in name. The 3D and models pages show the move's id and name as they are (D6, Chris's choice).
- Media stays in `.cache/video/` (git-ignored). Only `shots.json`, `shoot.mjs`, `build.py`, the `narrate` job and `speak()` are committed.

## Disclosure line (README and YouTube description)

> The narration in the demo video is a synthetic voice generated with Gemini text-to-speech (`gemini-3.8-flash-tts`). Every app shot is a screen capture of Pack It Up running on Nov 21, 2026, driven by a script; the title, results and end cards are plain text.

If D2 or D3 adds music or a generated opening, add: "Music generated with Lyria 3.5" or "The 4-second opening is generated video (Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash) and is labelled on screen."

## Numbers the video uses, and where they come from

All from [eval/RESULTS.md](../eval/RESULTS.md) as built at 14:50: 13 of 14 and 3 of 14 (table 1, "one per set"); move 133201 at 91.5 on two 26 ft trucks and 95.2 on one (table 2). The video says "mostly venue rooms" on screen and aloud, as that file's "What these tables do not show" asks. It quotes no inventory accuracy, no Decisions API grade and no truck-size-rule result, because each rests on one room or on our own room-as-bedroom assumption and needs more words than a minute allows. If `eval/results_table.py` is run again before the build, check that the "one per set" line still says 13 of 14 and 3 of 14; if not, change S7's line and card.
